scope: First journal repair final rejected disposition

JOURNAL-ACK-001.evidence: 18 fresh cases: OSError/ValueError deny False; KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit/GeneratorExit/custom BaseException propagate exact origin and reached frame at root-fstat/file-fstat/entry-stat. All begin with actual append/True ack; poison then denies later ack without a second binding visit and later writes refuse. Holding the cooperative lock after poisoning is observed, not treated as an error.

JOURNAL-OWNERSHIP-001.evidence: Returned close and failed constructor expose immutable snapshots, preserve primary origins and optional identity, attempt once and never retry. Real valid-fd/EBADF and independent-process flock observations support pre-release versus release-before-raise distinctions. New allocation-gap finding prevents unconditional constructor closure.
JOURNAL-OWNERSHIP-001.contract_migration_assessment: The migration is a genuine narrow observational handoff, not proof of physical release. Two independently owned normal-exit worker tests prove that a retained capsule accompanies a live blocked writer and kernel teardown releases it without manual descriptor close. This is operationally meaningful only where the caller/supervisor has separately established process ownership and a permitted controlled process boundary. No built-in supervisor, retry, kill or manager authority is present; capsule PID/inode/fd and forged snapshots cannot establish it. For a long-lived host lacking such a boundary, the unresolved status alone does not solve targeted cleanup.
JOURNAL-OWNERSHIP-001.old_oracle: Original unconditional zero-live-fd constructor oracle and failed report preserved and not rerun; no claim that they pass.
